claims.text: Increasing SPS consolidation temperature will improve the surface physical and mechanical properties of the coated components.
Using six ESD layers instead of three will improve the surface physical and mechanical properties of the coated components.
The listed higher SPS temperatures are 50 °C above the corresponding baseline temperatures.
Higher SPS temperatures enhance particle diffusion.
Higher SPS temperatures enhance alloying and homogenization.
Higher SPS temperatures promote pore closure and reduce porosity.
Higher SPS temperatures refine the microstructure.
Increasing the ESD layer count to six increases coating continuity.
Increasing the ESD layer count may increase oxidation and microfissuring.
Improved diffusion and alloying produce a more coherent and harder electrode material.
A six-layer ESD coating provides more complete substrate coverage and adhesion.
More complete coverage and adhesion strengthen the surface against aggressive environments.
The combined higher-temperature SPS and six-layer ESD intervention will yield higher density than lower-temperature SPS and three-layer ESD.
The combined intervention will yield lower porosity than the lower-temperature and three-layer baseline.
The combined intervention will increase coating hardness relative to the lower-temperature and three-layer baseline.
Six-layer coatings may have higher oxidation and roughness than three-layer coatings.
The benefits may not extend beyond six ESD layers because oxidation and microstructural degradation increase.
Preliminary trends support expected improvements in density and hardness.

contradictions.description: The intervention describes each higher SPS temperature as a 50 °C increase, but every listed intervention temperature is 100 °C above its listed baseline: 1050 versus 950 °C, 1000 versus 900 °C, and 950 versus 850 °C.
